parsed.explanation: Enforced trans-specific criminal exposure dominates: Article 266 punishes impersonating the opposite sex with 1 month–1 year, supplemented by indecency, morality and cyber-crime offences. Documented 2018–2020 arrests and multi-year combined sentences show active state enforcement, including against a foreign expatriate. A 2023 first-hand border incident—genderqueer visitor held separately, shirt removed and inappropriately touched—shows visitor-facing targeting, amplified by surveillance and digital-evidence prosecution. Advocacy is criminalised and no effective recourse is documented. No execution or custody-placement pattern is established, keeping this above the most severe tier, but imprisonment for presentation itself is a severe, state-imposed risk.
